bull_bear.body: Debt-free balance sheet; Merger of Timken GGB approved for synergies; Dividend reduced to INR 2.5/share (vs INR 36 previous special dividend) to prioritize reinvestment in growth projects.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material inflation outpacing price pass-through; Delay in PPAP approvals for new plants; Geopolitical trade tensions affecting exports; Cyclical downturn in CV/Tractor segments; Rail project execution delays.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on demand stability and long-term strategy; Cautious on near-term margins due to cost inflation; Aggressive on capacity utilization and price realization efforts.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Export growth to North America is accelerating (+66% YoY) despite pending trade deals; Process industry (Steel/Cement) expected to outpace Mobile/Rail in growth rate over next 2 years due to India's industrialization shift; Bharuch plant building cost was ~50% of total capex, allowing future expansion within existing structure.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Q4 Breakup: Rail 26% (INR 278 cr); Mobile (CV+Tractor) 19% (INR 205 cr); Process Industry 19% (INR 200 cr); Distribution 15% (INR 162 cr); Intercompany/Exports 21% (INR 222.5 cr). FY26 Total Revenue INR 3,419 cr.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising steel and input costs squeezing margins until price hikes are fully realized | Competitors with weaker pricing power | loser | Med | Timken's ability to pass on 90% of pending price hikes over 2 quarters may force smaller players to absorb costs, losing market share. |
| Need for high-precision, ultra-high-speed rail bearings for future projects | Domestic Rail OEMs | beneficiary | High | Jamshedpur expansion (live Dec FY26) specifically targets state-of-the-art robotics for super-precision rail bearings, reducing import dependence. |
| Energy security and cost optimization in manufacturing | Timken India (Self) | beneficiary | High | Completed renewable energy investments across plants provide long-term cost insulation against power tariff hikes. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Input costs (steel, grinding wheels, coolants) rising; Currency depreciation impacting imports; Price hike implementation started mid-April, only 10% realized so far, remaining 90% expected over next 2 quarters; Bharuch ramp-up costs near breakeven, impact reduced from Q3.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: > Market growth (no specific %); Margin: Under pressure short-term due to inflation, expecting recovery via price hikes over next 2 quarters; Order Inflow: Strong in North America exports and Process industry; Capex: ~8-10% of revenue annually (INR 120 cr for Jamshedpur rail expansion).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Described as 'healthy' with specific strength in North American exports (Q4 exports INR 222 cr, +40% QoQ) and domestic Rail (Q4 INR 278 cr).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Bharuch plant ramp-up (targeting 70% utilization by July FY27); Jamshedpur rail expansion going live by Dec FY26; Potential M&A; Expansion into larger bearing sizes and wind energy (5MW+).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Timken India crossed INR 1,000 crore quarterly revenue for the first time in Q4FY26, driven by robust exports and CV demand, though margins faced pressure from rising input costs with only 10% price pass-through achieved so far. The strategic merger with Timken GGB and progressive ramp-up of the Bharuch plant (targeting 70% utilization by July) position the company for long-term synergy, despite near-term margin volatility as cost hikes are negotiated.

open.item: The Board of Directors, subject to approval of Members at the ensuing AGM, has recommended a dividend of Rs 2.5 per equity share of Rs 10 each fully paid up for the financial year ended 31 March 2026.

The Company is investing approximately Rs 38 crores to set up a manufacturing line for plain bearings at Bharuch, to be sold under the brand name GGB, with commercial production expected to start during Q2 of FY 2026-27.

The Company is investing approximately Rs 120 crores to enhance capacity of bearing components (cup and cone) at the rail facility in Jamshedpur, expected to be completed in Q3 2026-27, with project work going on as per timelines.
The Board has approved a draft Scheme of Amalgamation involving amalgamation of Timken GGB Technology Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, with the Company.
The Bharuch manufacturing facility, inaugurated during the year and capitalized in FY 2025-26, continues to ramp up with the Company incurring initial operating costs and funding capability building.
The Company is making investments at the Bharuch facility to produce plain bearings using Fiber reinforced composite (FRC) material to strengthen its position in the plain bearing market.
The Company continues with its expansion with investment in the Jamshedpur Rail project.

risks.note: Global activity faces a major test from the outbreak of war in the Middle East, with global growth forecast to decelerate to 3.1 percent in 2026 from 3.4 percent in 2025 and a larger net impact expected on emerging markets; the Chairman also describes an environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties, evolving trade dynamics and changing industrial supply chains
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and slowing global growth

risks.note: India meets more than 85 percent of its crude oil requirements through imports with approximately half transiting the Strait of Hormuz, so the conflict poses the risk of a significant terms-of-trade shock that could increase input costs, exert downward pressure on the rupee, and complicate inflation-growth trade-offs

Profit before tax as a percentage of revenue from operations declined compared with the previous year mainly due to increased cost of material consumed, increased depreciation charges and reduction in other income, with net material cost rising modestly faster than revenue growth

Bringing a new site online requires patience and perseverance; as Bharuch ramps up the Company continues to incur initial operating costs and fund capability building, and higher depreciation from the new manufacturing plant added to other expenses
risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up drag from the new Bharuch plant

risks.note: Demand is tied to government capex and industry cycles — Indian Railways budgetary support, steel and cement capacity expansion, thermal PowerGen commissioning, mining output targets and infrastructure-led commercial vehicle demand — so any slowdown in public capex directly affects the bearing demand base
risks.risk: Cyclicality and policy dependence of end markets

risks.note: The record FY 2026 tractor upcycle was partly driven by pre-buying ahead of TREM V norms effective April 2026, which can borrow volumes from the following year even as the CV cycle is expected to moderate to efficiency-driven growth in FY 27
risks.risk: Pull-forward of tractor demand ahead of TREM V norms

risks.note: The Company runs material arm's length transactions with group entities — The Timken Company (Ultimate Holding Company, including royalty), The Timken Corporation and Timken Wuxi Bearings Co. Ltd. (fellow subsidiaries) — for purchases and sales of goods, making sourcing, offtake and technology access dependent on the parent group and requiring recurring Board and shareholder approvals

Revenue growth for the year was primarily driven by strong export sales with volume growth across geographical locations while domestic revenue showed modest growth, leaving the Company exposed to higher trade barriers and reconfiguration of trade flows and supply chains
